chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from 'Abdullah from al-Hasan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'If a man frees his concubine, is it permissible for him to marry her without a waiting period?' He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'And if it is someone else?' He said, 'No, until she observes a waiting period of three months.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a freed concubine if she marries her former owner versus another man?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the 'iddah of manumission (three months) and the 'iddah of marriage, ruling that a master who frees his concubine and immediately marries her is exempt from the waiting period due to the continuity of possession. This ruling highlights the specific juristic status of the concubine in early Islamic society, where her transition from slave to free wife within the same household did not require the separation period mandated for other women.
